chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father sold a piece of land belonging to Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik for such and such thousand dinars, and he stipulated upon him the zakat of that wealth for ten years, and he did that only because Hisham was the governor.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir stipulate the payment of zakat for ten years when buying land from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), purchased land from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, the Umayyad governor, and stipulated that the zakat on that wealth be paid for ten years. This was done specifically because Hisham, as the ruling authority, had the right to collect zakat during his tenure. This transaction highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams in navigating political realities, ensuring religious obligations were fulfilled while acknowledging the de facto authority of the Umayyad caliphate to prevent dispute or confiscation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin mahboub, from Abdullah bbin Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Myasws fatherasws was sold from Hisham Bin Abdul Malik a land of his for such and such thousand Dinars, and heasws stipulated upon him the Zakāt of that wealth for ten years, and rather heasws did that because Hisham, he was the governor’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘My father purchased a piece of land from Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik for such and such hundred thousand dinar with a condition that he will pay its Zakat for ten years. He did it as such because Hisham was the ruler.’”
